TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن سعد بن عبيدة وأبي عبد الرحمن السلمي
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.claim: When asked what work means if everything is decreed, the Prophet says to act because each person is facilitated for the easier or harder path.
TAB-FULL:v24p471/r3.anchor: اعملوا فكل ميسر: سنيسره لليسرى، وسنيسره للعسرى

NAHHAS:v4p298/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p298/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p298/r12.claim: The verse demonstrates that people are punished for disbelief in divine decree.
NAHHAS:v4p298/r12.anchor: فدل بهذا على أنهم يعذبون على كفرهم بالقدر

NAHHAS:v4p298/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p298/r13.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p298/r13.claim: Sibawayh explains the accusative كل by analogy with the fronted object in زيدا ضربته.
NAHHAS:v4p298/r13.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن نصب كل على لغة من قال زيدا ضربته

NAHHAS:v4p298/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p298/r14.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v4p298/r14.claim: The Kufans say إنا calls for a verb, which is more appropriate than a noun here, yielding the sense “We created everything.”
NAHHAS:v4p298/r14.anchor: أما الكوفيون فقالوا إنا تطلب الفعل والفعل بها أولى من الاسم والمعنى إنا خلقنا كل شيء

NAHHAS:v4p298/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p298/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p298/r15.claim: A third analysis says the accusative, unlike زيدا ضربته, highlights that all things are created and refutes deniers of created acts.
NAHHAS:v4p298/r15.anchor: والقول الثالث أنه إنما جاز هذا بالنصب وخالف زيد ضربته ليدل ذلك على خلق الأشياء

SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r1.claim: The common reading has كل accusative as الاشتغال; Abu al-Sammal reads it nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r1.anchor: العامة على نصب " كل " على الاشتغال وأبو السمال بالرفع

SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r2.claim: Some grammarians prefer or require accusative كل because nominative can imply that things not created by God are not measured by Him.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r2.anchor: رجح الناس، بل بعضهم أوجب النصب قال: لأن الرفع يوهم ما لا يجوز على قواعد أهل السنة

SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa says accusative signals universal creation, while nominative only says that every created thing is measured.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r3.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " وإنما كان النصب أولى لدلالته على عموم الخلق، والرفع لا يدل على عمومه

SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r4.speaker: مكي بن أبي طالب
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r4.claim: Makki says Basran principles favor nominative, like Zayd I struck him, while Kufan principles favor accusative after إن.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r4.anchor: وقال مكي بن أبي طالب: " كان الاختيار على أصول البصريين رفع " كل " كما أن الاختيار عندهم

SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r5.claim: The accusative reading is said to indicate that all created things belong to God, against claims of creation apart from Him.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r5.anchor: ليدل ذلك على عموم الأشياء المخلوقات أنها لله تعالى بخلاف ما قاله أهل الزيغ من أن ثم مخلوقات لغير الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r6.speaker: أهل الزيغ
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r6.claim: Some opponents claim that there are creatures not created by God.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r6.anchor: بخلاف ما قاله أهل الزيغ من أن ثم مخلوقات لغير الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r7.claim: An adjective cannot govern a word before its antecedent, which rules out taking خلقناه as an adjective of شيء.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r7.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون " خلقناه " صفة ل " شيء " لأن الصفة والصلة لا يعملان فيما قبل الموصوف

SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r8.claim: An adjective or relative clause also cannot explain a governor that precedes its antecedent.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r8.anchor: ولا يكونان تفسيرا لما يعمل فيما قبلهما، فإذا لم يبق " خلقناه " صفة

SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r9.claim: Under the nominative parse, بقدر is the predicate of كل, creating the restrictive implication discussed by grammarians.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49/r9.anchor: و " بقدر " خبره. وحينئذ يكون له مفهوم لا يخفى على متأمله

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports that some Sunnis read كل nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r1.anchor: ابن عطية:/ " وقوم من أهل السنة بالرفع "

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r2.speaker: أبو الفتح
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Fath calls nominative the stronger Arabic construction, although his own reading is accusative with the community.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو الفتح: " هو الوجه في العربية، وقراءتنا بالنصب مع الجماعة "

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses accusative كل as governed by an implicit verb explained by the overt verb; nominative was also read.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " كل شيء " منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر. وقرىء " كل شيء " بالرفع

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari notes that both qadar and qadr readings occur.

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes qadar or qadr as wise, ordered determination, or something written in the Preserved Tablet and known before it occurs.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r5.anchor: أي: خلقنا كل شيء مقدرا محكما مرتبا على حسب ما اقتضته الحكمة

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r6.claim: Al-Samin says al-Zamakhshari did not side with the Mu'tazila here because the nominative construction is weak.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r6.anchor: وهو هنا لم يتعصب للمعتزلة لضعف وجه الرفع

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r7.claim: When a following verb could look adjectival though the intended predicate is the verb, accusative on the first noun removes that ambiguity; nominative here suggests the wrong parse.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r7.anchor: اختير النصب في الاسم الأول حتى يتضح أن الفعل ليس بوصف، ومنه هذا الموضع

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r8.speaker: أهل السنة
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r8.claim: Sunnis infer from the accusative reading that God created everything by decree.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r8.anchor: وقد تنازع أهل السنة والقدرية الاستدلال بهذه الآية: فأهل السنة يقولون

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r9.speaker: القدرية
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r9.claim: Qadaris read كل nominative and خلقناه as its adjective, understanding that what God created is measured in form and time.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r9.anchor: وقال القدرية: القراءة برفع " كل " و " خلقناه " في موضع الصفة ل " كل "

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r10.speaker: بعض العلماء
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r10.claim: Qadar may mean measure in an entity's essence and attributes.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r10.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: في القدر هنا وجوه، أحدها: أنه المقدار في ذاته وفي صفاته

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r11.speaker: بعض العلماء
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r11.claim: Qadar may mean determining, as in 77:23.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r11.anchor: والثاني: التقدير كقوله فقدرنا فنعم القادرون

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r12.speaker: بعض العلماء
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r12.claim: Qadar may mean the decree paired with divine decision; the cited poet uses it for what has been determined.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r12.anchor: والثالث: القدر الذي يقال مع القضاء كقولك: كان بقضاء الله وقدره

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r13.claim: A cited poet uses قدر to mean something determined.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r13.anchor: وقد قدر الرحمن ما هو قادر أي: ما هو مقدر

SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r14.claim: بقدر is governed by the verb on the accusative reading and is the predicate of كل on the nominative reading.
SAMIN-DURR:54:49#2/r14.anchor: فقوله " بقدر " على قراءة النصب متعلق بالفعل الناصب وفي قراءة الرفع في محل رفع

ZAJJAJ:v5p92/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p92/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p92/r3.claim: Everything God created was decreed and written in the Preserved Tablet before it occurred.
ZAJJAJ:v5p92/r3.anchor: أي كل ما خلقنا فمقدورمكتوب في اللوح المحفوظ قبل وقوعه.

ZAJJAJ:v5p92/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p92/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p92/r4.claim: Kulla shayʾ is accusative under an understood verb: “We created every thing that We created according to a measure.”
ZAJJAJ:v5p92/r4.anchor: بفعل مضمر، المعنى إنا خلقنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر.

ASAD-NOTES:54:49/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:49/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:54:49/r1.claim: Everything is created according to due measure and proportion.
ASAD-NOTES:54:49/r1.anchor: everything have We created in due measure and proportion

IBNHIBBAN:6139/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6139/r1.speaker: author
IBNHIBBAN:6139/r1.claim: Ibn Ḥibbān frames the passage as God's reproach of those who opposed the Messenger regarding affirmation of divine decree.
IBNHIBBAN:6139/r1.anchor: كان مشركو قريش عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخالفونه

IBNHIBBAN:6139/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6139/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNHIBBAN:6139/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Quraysh's polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, and this revelation comprised 54:47–49, including the declaration that all things are created by decree.
IBNHIBBAN:6139/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال كان مشركو قريش عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخالفونه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p99/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p99/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p99/r1.claim: The closing section directly warns Quraysh to learn from earlier messengers’ nations: they will share their worldly humiliation and face worse in the next world, while the ending briefly mentions the God-fearing’s reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p99/r1.anchor: reward which those who remained fearful to God will receive.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p101/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p101/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p101/r7.claim: Punishment and Judgment are certain, but their timing follows a measure: God gives everything a defined duration suited to the purpose for which it was created.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p101/r7.anchor: God has created everything with a special measure and set a definite time period for everything

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p101/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p101/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p101/r8.claim: God applies the same measured pattern to nations, granting a rebellious people respite to develop its good and evil capacities until truth is fully established and it has no excuse; Quraysh receive the respite required by this law.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p101/r8.anchor: If a nation becomes rebellious, He does not seize it at once; He gives it enough respite

IBNMAJAH:83/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:83/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNMAJAH:83/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, verses 54:48–49 were revealed.
IBNMAJAH:83/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ جَاءَ مُشْرِكُو قُرَيْشٍ يُخَاصِمُونَ النَّبِيَّ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ فِي الْقَدَرِ

MUSLIM:6753/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:6753/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSLIM:6753/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, after which 54:48–49 were revealed.
MUSLIM:6753/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ جَاءَ مُشْرِكُو قُرَيْشٍ يُخَاصِمُونَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r10.claim: Most read كل شيء in the accusative; Abū al-Sammāl reads it nominative, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya and some Sunnis report, and Abū al-Fatḥ judges that more idiomatic, while Abū Ḥayyān notes the communal accusative reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r10.anchor: قراءة الجمهور: كل شيء بالنصب. وقرأ أبو السمال، قال ابن عطية وقوم من أهل السنة: بالرفع. قال أبو الفتح: هو الوجه في العربية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r11.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r11.claim: Some prefer the accusative when the verb might be mistaken for an adjective and a later element could be a predicate, clarifying that the verb itself is the predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r11.anchor: وقال قوم: إذا كان الفعل يتوهم فيه الوصف، وأن ما بعده يصلح للخبر، وكان المعنى على أن يكون الفعل هو الخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r12.speaker: أهل السنة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r12.claim: Sunnis use the accusative reading to argue that every thing is created by God through His power, since this parsing makes the verb the predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r12.anchor: فأهل السنة يقولون: كل شيء فهو مخلوق لله تعالى بقدرة دليله قراءة النصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r13.speaker: القدرية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r13.claim: The Qadariyya use the nominative reading, parsing خلقناه as an adjective of كل; everything God created is measured in form, time, and other respects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r13.anchor: وقالت القدرية: القراءة برفع كل، وخلقناه في موضع الصفة لكل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses accusative كل as governed by an omitted verb explained by the overt verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p47/r14.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: كل شيء منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r1.claim: Two vocalizations, qadr and qadar, are reported for the word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r1.anchor: بهما، أي خلقنا كل شيء مقدرا محكما مرتبا على حسب ما اقتضته الحكمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r2.claim: The readings can mean that everything was measured precisely and arranged according to wisdom, or predetermined, written in the Tablet, and known before it existed with its state and time known.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r2.anchor: مقدرا محكما مرتبا على حسب ما اقتضته الحكمة، أو مقدرا مكتوبا في اللوح، معلوما قبل كونه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r3.claim: One proposed sense of qadr is the measure of each thing's essence and attributes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r3.anchor: أن يكون بمعنى المقدار في ذاته وصفاته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r4.claim: Another sense is determination: the source cites 77:23 and an unnamed poet's line وما قدر الرحمن ما هو قادر to show the sense of what is decreed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r4.anchor: والثاني: التقدير، قال تعالى: فقدرنا فنعم القادرون . وقال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r5.claim: A third sense pairs qadar with qaḍāʾ: qaḍāʾ is what is in divine knowledge and qadar what is in divine will, so the phrase means creation by power together with will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p48/r5.anchor: أن القضاء ما في العلم، والقدر ما في الإرادة، فالمعنى في الآية: خلقناه بقدر: أي بقدرة مع إرادة

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9736/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9736/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9736/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, after which the passage about everything being created by measure was revealed.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9736/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: " جاء مشركو قريش إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاصمونه في القدر، فنزلت

MUSNAD-AHMAD:10164/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10164/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10164/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet and that the verses about Hell and God's measure were revealed.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10164/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: جاء مشركو قريش يخاصمون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في القدر، فنزلت هذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r1.claim: God created every created thing by measure, written in the Preserved Tablet before occurring; qadar here has its familiar sense contrasted with qaḍāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r1.anchor: مكتوبا في اللوحقبلوقوعه فالقدر بالمعنى المشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r2.speaker: كثير من السلف
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r2.claim: This interpretation of qadar as predestination is transmitted from many early authorities.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r2.anchor: هو المأثور عن كثير من السلف

ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, whereupon the verses about being dragged into Hell and creation by measure were revealed; Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah transmit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : جاء مشركو قريش يخاصمون رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r4.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet’s statement that the Murjiʾa and Qadariyya have no share in Islam and that verses beginning ‘the sinners are in error and fire’ concern them; al-Tirmidhi grades it ḥasan.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r4.anchor: عنابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas strongly disliked the Qadariyya; Abu Yahya al-Aʿraj heard him threaten them and say adultery, theft, and drinking wine occur by decree.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p93#4/r5.anchor: عن أبي يحيى الأعرج قال سمعتابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r1.claim: Mujahid asked Ibn Abbas what he would do to someone denying predestination; Ibn Abbas said to bring the person so he could choke him to death.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال : قلتلابن عباس : ما تقول فيمن يكذب بالقدر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r2.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r2.claim: The Prophet calls deniers of decree the Magians of his community and says not to visit them when ill or attend their funerals; Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tabarani transmit from Ibn Umar.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمران أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : لكل أمة مجوس

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r3.claim: Alternatively, creation by measure means each thing was precisely fashioned in accord with the wisdom governing creation, as in 25:2.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r3.anchor: وجوز كون المعنى إنا كل شي خلقناه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r4.claim: With the transmitted accusative, كل is governed by a verb understood from the following verb: ‘We created every thing.’
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r4.anchor: ونصب ( كل ) بفعل يفسره ما بعدهأي إنا خلقنا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r5.claim: The verse establishes that everything created is measured; ‘every thing’ means every created thing, not all infinitely many possibles, which God did not create.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r5.anchor: على أن كل شيء مخلوق بقدر ولا ينبغي أن تجعل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r6.speaker: أبو السمال وابن عطية وقوم من أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r6.claim: Abu al-Sammal, as Ibn Atiyya notes, and a group of Sunnis read كل in the nominative; it is then a subject, with خلقناه as predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r6.anchor: وقرا أبو السمال قال : ابن عطية وقوممن أهل السنة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r7.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r7.claim: Al-Raḍi says the readings need not differ: كل refers to created things in either parse, so every thing God created is measured.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r7.anchor: وقال الرضي : لا يتفاوتالمعنى لأن مراده تعالى بكل شيء كل مخلوق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r8.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r8.claim: Al-Raḍi distinguishes the predicate parse (‘every thing We created is measured’) from the adjectival parse (‘every thing created by Us is measured’), but sees both as restricted to created things.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r8.anchor: خلقناه هو الخبر ( كل ) مخلوق مخلوق ( بقدر )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r9.speaker: السيد السند
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r9.claim: Al-Sayyid al-Sanad objects that the adjectival parse leaves room for other created things outside the ruling, unlike predicate or accusative parses; the sentence does not communicate that they share the attribute.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r10.speaker: الشهاب الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r10.claim: Al-Shihab al-Khafaji makes a similar objection; al-Alusi concludes that the accusative reading states the intended meaning most explicitly and outweighs a potentially misleading nominative parse despite requiring ellipsis.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p94/r10.anchor: وذكر نحوه الشهاب الخفاجي ولكونالنصب نصافي المقصود

TIRMIDHI:2157/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:2157/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TIRMIDHI:2157/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet and 54:49 was revealed; the segment also quotes 54:48. Tirmidhi grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
TIRMIDHI:2157/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ جَاءَ مُشْرِكُو قُرَيْشٍ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُخَاصِمُونَ فِي الْقَدَرِ

TIRMIDHI:3290/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3290/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TIRMIDHI:3290/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet and 54:49 was revealed; the segment also quotes 54:48. Tirmidhi grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
TIRMIDHI:3290/r1.anchor: قَالَ جَاءَ مُشْرِكُو قُرَيْشٍ يُخَاصِمُونَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي الْقَدَرِ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r1.claim: Everything God creates is measured and recorded in the Preserved Tablet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r1.anchor: أي: ما خلقناه فمقدور ومكتوب في اللوح المحفوظ،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r2.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says God assigned each created thing the measure appropriate to it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: قدر الله لكل شيء من خلقه قدره الذي ينبغي له.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, and verses 54:47–49 were revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: جاءت مشركو قريش إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاصمونه في القدر فنزلت هذه الآية: "إن المجرمين في ضلال وسعر"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r4.claim: The Prophet said God wrote the destinies of creatures fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth, while His Throne was upon the water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "كتب الله مقادير الخلائق قبل أن يخلق السموات والأرض بخمسين ألف سنة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r5.speaker: طاووس اليماني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r5.claim: Tawus says he met Companions of the Prophet who affirmed that everything is by God’s decree.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r5.anchor: عن طاووس اليماني قال: أدركت ناسا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقولون: "كل شيء بقدر الله"،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r6.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying that everything, including incapacity and ability, is by decree.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p435/r6.anchor: وسمعت عبد الله بن [عمر] (5) رضي الله عنه يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كل شيء بقدر حتى العجز والكيس،

BAYDAWI-FULL:54:46-49/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:46-49/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:46-49/r6.claim: Everything is created to a measure and order suited to wisdom, or measured and written in the Preserved Tablet before it occurs.

BAYDAWI-FULL:54:46-49/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:46-49/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:46-49/r7.claim: In the accusative reading, كل شيء is object of a verb explained by what follows; in the nominative it is the subject and خلقناه its predicate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:46-49/r7.anchor: وكل شيء منصوب بفعل يفسره ما بعده

BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r1.claim: After describing Judgment, the author says God's decree encompasses everything, including disbelievers' persistence; some wrongly infer God approves their conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r1.anchor: ولما أخبر بقيام الساعة وما يتفق لهم فيها جزاء لأعمالهم التي قدرها عليهم وهي ستر فرضوا بها لاتباع الشهوات

BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r2.claim: God created every small and great thing according to fixed measure: decree, judgment, proportion, bounded allotment, governance, and planning at a set time and place, written in the Preserved Tablet and measured by angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r2.anchor: أي قضاء وحكم وقياس مضبوط وقسمة محدودة وقودة بالغة وتدبير محكم في وقت معلوم ومكان محدود مكتوب في ذلك اللوح

BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r3.claim: The accusative in كل شيء signals universal scope; the following clause resumes the omitted governing verb and describes creation as precisely ordered.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r3.anchor: استأنف قوله تفسيرا للعامل المطوي وإخبارا بجعل ذلك الخلق كله على نظام محكم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r4.claim: The author rebukes people who accepted sinful acts as God's will and then used it to excuse themselves, quoting their claim that God would not have allowed idolatry if He wished otherwise.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p366/r4.anchor: فاصبروا عليه وارضوا به كما كنتم ترضون أعمالكم السيئة ثم تحتجون على عبادنا بأنها مشيئتنا بنحو

DURR-FULL:v7p682/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p682/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v7p682/r4.claim: Quraysh polytheists disputed divine decree with the Prophet, and the passage ending with this verse was revealed in response.
DURR-FULL:v7p682/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: جاء مشركو قريش إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاصمونه في القدر فنزلت

DURR-FULL:v7p682/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p682/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v7p682/r5.claim: A good-chain report through Amr ibn Shuaib from his father and grandfather says this verse was revealed only about the deniers of divine decree.
DURR-FULL:v7p682/r5.anchor: من طريق عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده قال: ما أنزلت هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v7p682/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p682/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p682/r6.claim: The Prophet recited the verse and applied it to people in a later age of his community who deny God's decree.
DURR-FULL:v7p682/r6.anchor: عن زرارة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه تلا هذه الآية {ذوقوا مس سقر إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر} قال: في أناس من أمتي في آخر الزمان

DURR-FULL:v7p683/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identified the Qadariyya as the verse's subject, called them the worst of the community, and forbade visiting their sick or attending their dead.
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قيل له: قد تكلم في القدر فقال: أو فعلوها والله ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا فيهم

DURR-FULL:v7p683/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says these verses were revealed concerning the Qadariyya.
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: نزلت هذه الآية في القدرية {يوم يسحبون في النار على وجوههم ذوقوا مس سقر إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر}

DURR-FULL:v7p683/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God created all creation according to a decree and created good and evil according to a decree.
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r5.anchor:
عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر}
قال: خلق الله الخلق كلهم بقدر وخلق لهم الخير والشر بقدر

DURR-FULL:v7p683/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r6.claim: The Prophet said that everything occurs by divine decree, including incapacity and ability.
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كل شيء بقضاء وقدر حتى العجز والكيس

DURR-FULL:v7p683/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas said everything is by decree, even putting one's hand on one's cheek.
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كل شيء بقضاء وقدر حتى وضعك يدك على خدك

DURR-FULL:v7p683/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r8.claim: The Prophet called those who deny predestination this community's Magians and said not to visit their sick or attend their funerals.
DURR-FULL:v7p683/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لكل أمة مجوس ومجوس أمتي الذين يقولون لا قدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p215/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p215/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p215/r12.claim: The statement about criminals' error and fire concludes the preceding threats and lessons from the punished deniers, and prepares for the claim that God's command is one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p215/r12.anchor: استئناف وقع تذييلا لما قبله من الوعيد والإنذار والاعتبار بما حل بالمكذبين ، وهو أيضا توطئة لقوله : { وما أمرنا إلا واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r1.claim: The emphatic particle إن here is explained as it was in the earlier statement about criminals in error and fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r1.anchor: يقال فيه ما قلناه في قوله : إن المجرمين في ضلال وسعر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r2.claim: خلق literally means deliberately bringing entities into existence and can metaphorically mean producing distinct, clear meanings; the verse uses the term in both senses, as in 29:17.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r2.anchor: والخلق أصله : إيجاد ذات بشكل مقصود فهو حقيقة في إيجاد الذوات ، ويطلق مجازا على إيجاد المعاني التي تشبه الذوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r3.claim: شيء encompasses every existent, both substances and accidents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r3.anchor: و { شيء } معناه موجود من الجواهر والأعراض ، أي خلقنا كل الموجودات جواهرها وأعراضها بقدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r4.claim: قدر with a moving د is synonymous with قدر with a quiescent د and means setting, measuring, and determining things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r4.anchor: والقدر : بتحريك الدال مرادف القدر بسكونها وهو تحديد الأمور وضبطها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r5.claim: God creates all things under ordered laws governed by wisdom; the universal scope includes Hell as punishment, and Quranic accounts connect purposeful creation with the Day of Judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r5.anchor: والمراد : أن خلق الله الأشياء مصاحب لقوانين جارية على الحكمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r6.claim: The verse concludes the surah's warnings by grounding punishment in purposeful creation, between the reminder that the disbelievers are no better than earlier peoples and the coming mention of their kindred's destruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r6.anchor: فهذا وجه تعقيب آيات الإنذار والعقاب المذكورة في هذه السورة بالتذييل بقوله : { إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر } بعد قوله : { أكفاركم خير من أولائكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r7.claim: The ب is for circumstantial accompaniment, and the phrase is a stable adjunct functioning like a second object of خلقناه because the measure itself is the intended point.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r7.anchor: فالباء في { بقدر } للملابسة ، والمجرور ظرف مستقر ، فهو في حكم المفعول الثاني لفعل { خلقناه } لأنه مقصود بذاته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r8.claim: The point is God's knowledge and wisdom in recompense, not merely that He created everything; that bare fact would not need such emphatic assertion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p216/r8.anchor: إذ ليس المقصود الإعلام بأن كل شيء مخلوق لله ، فإن ذلك لا يحتاج إلى الإعلام به بله تأكيده بل المقصود إظهار معنى العلم والحكمة في الجزاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r1.claim: The verse does not settle whether human acts are created by God, as the Muʿtazilites hold, or acquired by people, as the Ashʿarites hold: its scope and point admit several readings. This does not negate qadar proved elsewhere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r1.anchor: فلا حجة بالآية عليهم لاحتمال أن يكون مصب الإخبار هو مضمون { خلقناه } أو مضمون { بقدر } ، ولاحتمال عموم { كل شيء } للتخصيص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r2.claim: The technical reality of qadar is hidden: human knowledge cannot unravel how God's direction, causal means, obstacles, and human capacity for action affect created things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r2.anchor: وحقيقة القدر الاصطلاحي خفية فإن مقدار تأثر الكائنات بتصرفات الله تعالى وبتسبب أسبابها ونهوض موانعها لم يبلغ علم الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r3.claim: Good and evil deeds alike are subject to God's will and power; attributing good to Him while withholding attribution of evil is reverence taught to servants, not a denial of His governance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r3.anchor: والأدلة الشرعية والعقلية تقتضي أن الأعمال الصالحة والأعمال السيئة سواء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r4.claim: The Prophet teaches belief in qadar, both its good and its evil; Abu Dawud also transmits through Ibn ʿUmar a Prophetic report calling the Qadariyya the Magians of this community.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r4.anchor: لقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( وتؤمن بالقدر خيره وشره ) ، وقوله : ( القدرية مجوس هذه الأمة ) رواه أبو داود بسنده إلى ابن عمر مرفوعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r5.claim: كل شيء is the object of خلقناه by the الاشتغال construction; fronting its explicit noun before its pronoun reinforces the object, in addition to إن reinforcing the statement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r5.anchor: وانتصب { كل شيء } على المفعولية ل { خلقناه } على طريقة الاشتغال ، وتقديمه على { خلقناه } ليتأكد مدلوله بذكر اسمه الظاهر ابتداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r6.claim: The word order keeps بقدر next to its verb so it cannot be mistaken for an adjective meaning 'every measured thing'; that alternative would also leave إن's predicate pending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p218#2/r6.anchor: وليتصل قوله : { بقدر } بالعامل فيه وهو { خلقناه } ، لئلا يلتبس بالنعت لشيء لو قيل : إنا خلقنا كل شيء بقدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r2.claim: Most readers put kull in the accusative, understanding an implied verb: We created every thing that we created according to a measure; khalaqnāhu is not an adjective of shayʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r2.anchor: فقرأ جمهور الناس: «إنا كل» بالنصب، والمعنى: خلقنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r3.claim: The accusative reading means everything is created, except what rational proof establishes as uncreated, such as the Quran and divine attributes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r3.anchor: وهذا المعنى يقتضي أن كل شيء مخلوق، إلا ما قام دليل العقل على أنه ليس بمخلوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r4.speaker: أبو السمال وأبو الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r4.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads kull in the nominative as a subject with khalaqnāhu bi-qadar as its predicate; Abū al-Fatḥ prefers this reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال ورجحه أبو الفتح: «إنا كل» بالرفع على الابتداء، والخبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r5.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r5.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls the nominative construction the best grammatical form, though he and his community read the accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r5.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: هذا هو الوجه في العربية، وقراءتنا بالنصب مع جماعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r6.speaker: أهل السنة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r6.claim: Sunnis read the nominative as saying that everything is created according to a prior measure; they do not take khalaqnāhu as an adjective, and see a strong proof in either reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r6.anchor: وقرأها قوم من أهل السنة بالرفع، والمعنى عندهم على نحو ما عند الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r7.speaker: القدرية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r7.claim: The Qadariyya deny divine predetermination and say each person alone creates their acts; they construe khalaqnāhu as an adjective so that the verse does not prove their acts are predetermined.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r7.anchor: وقالت القدرية وهم الذين يقولون: لا قدر، والمرء فاعل وحده أفعاله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r9.claim: Abū Hurayra says Quraysh disputed with the Messenger about qadar, and this verse was revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r9.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: خاصمت قريش رسول الله في القدر فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r10.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r10.claim: A man asked whether deeds begin anew or are already decreed; the Prophet said to act, since each person is facilitated toward what they were created for, citing ease or hardship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r10.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي: فقال رجل يا رسول الله ففيم العمل؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r11.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r11.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that Qadariyya, who claim good and evil are in our hands, have no share in his intercession and that he disowns them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p221/r11.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «القدرية يقولون الخير والشر بأيدينا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r3.claim: God creates everything according to a measure and guides creatures to the measure assigned to them, as also stated in 25:2 and 87:1–3.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r3.anchor: أي: قدر قدرا، وهدى الخلائق إليه؛ ولهذا يستدل بهذه الآية الكريمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r4.claim: Sunni imams use this and similar verses and sound hadiths to establish God's prior decree: He knew things before they existed and wrote them before creating them, against the Qadariyya, who arose late in the Companions' era.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r4.anchor: إثبات قدر الله السابق لخلقه، وهو علمه الأشياء قبل كونها وكتابته لها قبل برئها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed with the Prophet about decree, and these verses were then revealed; Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء مشركو قريش إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاصمونه في القدر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r6.speaker: جد عمرو بن شعيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r6.claim: The grandfather of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb says these verses came down only concerning the people who deny decree; al-Bazzar transmits the report without stating a grade.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p482#2/r6.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: ما نزلت هذه الآيات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r1.claim: A report traced to the Prophet says the verses were revealed about people in the latter days of the community who deny God's decree; no grading is given.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه تلا هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r2.claim: When told people were discussing decree, Ibn Abbas said the verses concerned them, called them the worst of the community, forbade visiting their sick or praying over their dead, and threatened a denier.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r2.anchor: فوالله ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا فيهم: {ذوقوا مس سقر. إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas said he would seize a man denying decree, then cited the Prophet: women of Banu Fihr would circle Khazraj as polytheists, the community's first shirk; their error would end in denying that God decrees good as well as evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r3.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "كأني بنساء بني فهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r4.claim: Ibn Umar warned a Syrian friend in a letter not to write to him after hearing that he discussed decree, because the Prophet foretold people in the community who would deny it; Abu Dawud transmits it from Ahmad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p483/r4.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "سيكون في أمتي أقوام يكذبون بالقدر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r1.claim: The Prophet called those who deny decree the community's Magians and said not to visit them when sick or attend their funerals; Ahmad transmits this route, which none of the six canonical compilers included.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لكل أمة مجوس، ومجوس أمتي الذين يقولون: لا قدر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r2.claim: The Prophet foretold metamorphosis among the community's deniers of decree and heretics; al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmit it, and al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih gharib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "سيكون في هذه الأمة مسخ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r3.claim: The Prophet said everything, including incapacity and cleverness, is by decree; Muslim alone transmits this report through Malik.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r3.anchor: عن طاوس اليماني قال: سمعت ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كل شيء بقدرن حتى العجز والكيس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r4.claim: A sound Prophetic hadith urges seeking God's help without helplessness, accepting events as God's decree and will, and avoiding if-only regrets because they open Satan's work.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r4.anchor: استعن بالله ولا تعجز، فإن أصابك أمر فقل: قدر الله وما شاء فعل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r5.claim: The Prophet told Ibn Abbas that all people together could not benefit or harm him beyond what God had decreed; the pens are dry and the scrolls folded.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r5.anchor: واعلم أن الأمة لو اجتمعوا على أن ينفعوك بشيء، لم يكتبه الله لك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r6.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r6.claim: On his deathbed, ʿUbada instructed his son that true faith and knowledge require belief in good and bad decree: what missed him could not have hit him and what hit him could not have missed; the first creation was the pen, commanded to write all that would be until Resurrection. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih gharib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p484/r6.anchor: إن أول ما خلق الله القلم. ثم قال له: اكتب. فجرى في تلك الساعة بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p485/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p485/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p485/r1.claim: The Prophet said a servant must believe in four matters: God's oneness, Muhammad's true prophethood, death, resurrection, and decree, good and bad; al-Tirmidhi considers the route through Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi the sounder, and Ibn Majah also transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p485/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يؤمن عبد حتى يؤمن بأربع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p485/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p485/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p485/r2.claim: God wrote the creatures' decrees 50,000 years before creating the heavens and earth; Ibn Wahb adds that God's Throne was then upon water. Muslim transmits it, and al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih gharib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p485/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله كتب مقادير الخلائق قبل أن يخلق السموات والأرض بخمسين ألف سنة

JISHUMI:v9p6698/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6698/r9.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v9p6698/r9.claim: The common reading makes كل accusative as the object, by fronting it as in the example زيدا ضربته.
JISHUMI:v9p6698/r9.anchor: قراءة العامة: (كل شيء) بنصبه اللام على تقدير أنه مفعول

JISHUMI:v9p6698/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6698/r10.speaker: أبو السمال العدوي
JISHUMI:v9p6698/r10.claim: Abu al-Samal al-Adawi reads كل in the nominative as the beginning of a sentence.
JISHUMI:v9p6698/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو [السمال] العدوي: كل بالرفع على الابتداء

BURSEVI:v9p231/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p231/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p231/r11.claim: “Everything” is accusative, governed by the verb explained by the following verb.
BURSEVI:v9p231/r11.anchor: من الأشياء وهو منصوب بفعل يفسره ما بعده

BURSEVI:v9p231/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p231/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p231/r12.claim: Each thing is created with a definite measure set by wisdom, shaping its form and outward and inward qualities for the benefit attached to its creation; alternatively it was prewritten in the Tablet before occurring.
BURSEVI:v9p231/r12.anchor: متعين اقتضته الحكمة التي عليها يدور أمر التكوين فقدر بمعنى التقدير وهو تسوية صورته وشكله

BURSEVI:v9p232/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p232/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p232/r1.claim: The Persian couplet evokes God’s settled decision and a dried pen, counseling silence before what has been inscribed on the eternal Tablet.
BURSEVI:v9p232/r1.anchor: قضى الله أمرا وجف القلم سر بر خط لوح ازلي دار وخموش

BURSEVI:v9p232/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p232/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p232/r2.claim: Bursevi distinguishes qada as all creation’s collective existence in the Preserved Tablet and qadar as its actual existence in the world once conditions arise.
BURSEVI:v9p232/r2.anchor: وهو القدر المستعمل في جنب القضاء بالقضاء وجود جميع المخلوقات في اللوح المحفوظ مجتمعة والقدر وجودها في الأعيان

BURSEVI:v9p232/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p232/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v9p232/r3.claim: The Prophet says God wrote all creatures’ destinies fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth, while His Throne was upon water.
BURSEVI:v9p232/r3.anchor: كتب الله مقادير الخلائق كلها قبل أن يخلق السموات والأرض بخمسين ألف سنة وعرشه على الماء

BURSEVI:v9p232/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p232/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v9p232/r4.claim: The Prophet says everything, including incapacity and cleverness, occurs by God’s decree.
BURSEVI:v9p232/r4.anchor: كل شيء بقدر الله حتى العجز والكيس

BURSEVI:v9p232/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p232/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v9p232/r5.claim: The Prophet names four required beliefs: God’s oneness, his own true apostleship, resurrection after death, and belief in destiny’s good and evil.
BURSEVI:v9p232/r5.anchor: لا يؤمن عبد حتى يأمن بأربع يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأني رسول الله بعثني بالحق

BURSEVI:v9p232/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p232/r6.speaker: أهل السنة
BURSEVI:v9p232/r6.claim: Ahl al-Sunna hold that good and evil are servants’ acts, for which they are rewarded or punished, yet occur by God’s will and decree; Bursevi says this refutes Qadariyya, Muʿtazila, and Kharijites.
BURSEVI:v9p232/r6.anchor: قال في كشف الأسرار مذهب أهل سنت آنست كه نيكى وبدى هرند فعل بنده است وبنده بدان مثاب ومعاقب است

BURSEVI:v9p232/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p232/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p232/r7.claim: The Najmiyya reading says every scientific and concrete existent was created eternally at a definite measure matching its original disposition and capacity, with nothing added or lacking.
BURSEVI:v9p232/r7.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية خلقنا كل شيء أي موجود علمي وعيني في الأزل بمقدار معين مثل ما قال

BURSEVI:v9p232/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p232/r8.speaker: الغزالي
BURSEVI:v9p232/r8.claim: Al-Ghazali says no possible world is more excellent than this one; otherwise its nonappearance would imply miserliness or incapacity in God.
BURSEVI:v9p232/r8.anchor: كما قال الغزالي رحمه الله ليس في الإمكان أبدع من هذا الوجود لأنه لو كان ولم يظهر لكان بخيلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r7.claim: Kulla shayʾin is accusative under an omitted verb explained by the following verb; a reading instead has nominative kulla shayʾin.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r8.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r8.claim: Both vocalizations, al-qadar and al-qadr, are read; both mean determination or measuring.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r9.claim: One explanation is that each thing was created measured, wise, and ordered according to what wisdom required.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r9.anchor: أي : خلقنا كل شيء مقدرا محكما مرتبا على حسب ما اقتضته الحكمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r10.claim: Another explanation is that each thing was measured and written in the Preserved Tablet, with its state and time known before it existed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p440/r10.anchor: أو مقدرا مكتوبا في اللوح . معلوما قبل كونه ، قد علمنا حاله وزمانه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r1.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says Quraysh disputed predestination with the Prophet, and this verse was revealed in response.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r1.anchor: روى إسماعيل بن زياد عن محمد بن عباد عن أبي هريرة أن مشركي قريش

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r2.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r2.claim: Ibn Bahr says God created everything according to His will, without addition or shortfall.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r2.anchor: على قدر ما أردنا من غير زيادة ولا نقصان ، قاله ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p419#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes qadar as a prior decree and an unavoidable judgment, supported by a rajaz line.

MUQATIL:54:46-51/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:54:46-51/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:54:46-51/r4.claim: God determined for them the punishment and entry into Saqar.
MUQATIL:54:46-51/r4.anchor: قدر الله لهم العذاب ودخول سقر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r1.claim: “Everything” is accusative as the object of an implicit verb explained by the following “We created”; the nominative reading is anomalous.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r1.anchor: كل منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر وقرى بالرفع شاذا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r2.claim: He prefers the accusative: with the nominative, “We created it” could modify “thing,” leaving “by measure” as predicate, or itself be the predicate.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r2.anchor: والنصب اول لانه لو رفع لامكن ان يكون خلقناه في موضع الجر وصفا لشىء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r3.claim: The accusative construction makes creation general to every thing, which is the verse's intended meaning; “We created” cannot be an adjective of “thing” because it explains the verb that governs it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r3.anchor: فيكون الخلق عاما لكل شىء وهو المراد بالاية ولا يجوز في النصب ان يكون خلقناه صفة لشىء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r4.claim: Bi-qadar can mean according to a prior decree, or that each thing is created precisely, in an ordered way that accords with wisdom.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r4.anchor: والقدر والقدر التقدير اى بتقدير سابق أو خلقنا كل شىء مقدرا محكما مرتبا على تحسب ما اقتضته الحكمة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r5.claim: Alternatively, every thing was measured and recorded in the Preserved Tablet, with its state and time known before it came to be.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r5.anchor: أو مقدرا مكتوبا في اللوح معلوما قبل كونه قد علما حاله ومانه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r6.claim: The verse continues the point that God's command is a single act, swift as a blink of an eye.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r6.anchor: وما أمرنا إلا واحدة كلمح بالبصر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r7.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, and this verse was revealed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r7.anchor: قال أبو هريرة جاء مشركوا قريش إلى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاصمونه في القدر فنزلت الاية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r8.speaker: عمر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r8.claim: ʿUmar used to swear that the verse was revealed concerning the Qadariyya.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p198#11/r8.anchor: وكان عمر يحلف انها نزلت في القدرية

QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة والنبي
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, after which the verses about being dragged into Hell and all things created by measure were revealed; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r2.anchor: في صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء مشركو قريش يخاصمون رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر والنبي
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r3.claim: Tawus heard Companions affirm that everything is decreed, then Ibn Umar quoted the Prophet: everything, including incapacity and competence, is by decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r3.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " كل شيء بقدر حتى العجز والكيس

QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r4.claim: The author presents the report as refuting the Qadariyya.

QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r5.speaker: أبو السمال
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r5.claim: The common reading puts kull in the accusative; Abu al-Sammal reads it nominatively as the subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال «كل» بالرفع على الابتداء.

QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r6.claim: The accusative supplies an implicit verb; the Kufans prefer it because inna calls for a verb, which it is more fitting to supply.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r6.anchor: ومن نصب فبإضمار فعل وهو اختيار الكوفيين لأن إن تطلب الفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r7.claim: The accusative better conveys universality; deleting the explanatory verb yields “We created every thing by measure,” while khalaqnāhu cannot modify or explain a preceding word.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r7.anchor: والنصب أدل على العموم في المخلوقات لله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r8.claim: Sunni teaching is that God knew each thing’s measure, state, and time before creating it, then creates what His prior knowledge specified.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r8.anchor: الذي عليه أهل السنة أن الله سبحانه قدر الأشياء أي علم مقاديرها وأحوالها

QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r9.claim: Every event proceeds from God’s knowledge, power, and will; people have only acquisition and effort, enabled through His power, guidance, and inspiration.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r9.anchor: فلا يحدث حدث في العالم العلوي والسفلي إلا وهو صادر عن علمه تعالى وقدرته

QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r10.claim: The author rejects the Qadari claim that human actions belong to us while lifespans belong to someone else; God alone creates.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:47-49/r10.anchor: لا كما قالت القدرية وغيرهم من أن الأعمال إلينا والآجال بيد غيرنا

QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r1.claim: Abu Dharr reports that a Najran delegation said actions were theirs and lifespans belonged to others; the verses through 54:49 came down, and the Prophet answered their objection about written sins and punishment by saying they would dispute with God on Judgment Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r1.anchor: قدم وفد نجران على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: الأعمال إلينا والآجال بيد غيرنا

QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله والنبي
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r2.claim: The Prophet calls deniers of divine decrees this community’s Magians and says not to visit their sick, attend their dead, or greet them; Ibn Majah transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر والنبي
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas and Jabir says two groups have no share in Islam: the Murjiʾa and the Qadariyya; Ibn Majah transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس وجابر قالا: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r4.speaker: أنس والنبي
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r4.claim: A report through al-Nahhas from Anas says Qadariyya who claim good and evil are in human hands have no share in the Prophet’s intercession and neither side belongs to the other.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r4.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r5.claim: Muslim reports Ibn Umar dissociating himself from the Qadariyya; the author infers he would dissociate only from unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r5.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم أن ابن عمر تبرأ منهم ولا يتبرأ إلا من كافر

QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r6.claim: Ibn Umar swears that even an Uhud-sized amount of gold spent by one of them would not be accepted until he believed in predestination.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r6.anchor: لو أن لأحدهم مثل أحد ذهبا فأنفقه ما قبل الله منه حتى يؤمن بالقدر.

QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r7.claim: The author links this rejection of unbelievers’ spending to 9:54, where disbelief in God and His Messenger prevents their contributions from being accepted.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r7.anchor: وهذا مثل قوله تعالى في المنافقين: وما منعهم أن تقبل منهم نفقاتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة والنبي
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that belief in predestination removes worry and grief.
QURTUBI-FULL:54:49/r8.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r1.claim: Most exegetes say the verse was revealed concerning the Qadariyya.
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين اتفقوا على أنها نازلة في القدرية

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed the doctrine of qadar with the Prophet, after which verses 54:47–49 were revealed; Razi gives no grading.

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says this verse was revealed about the Qadariyya; Razi states no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r3.anchor: نقل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن هذه الآية نزلت في القدرية

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r4.speaker: عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r4.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet calling the Qadariyya the Magi of this community; Razi states no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r4.anchor: وروي عن عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r5.speaker: الجبري
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r5.claim: Jabriyya call those who deny that obedience and sin are created by God's decree the Qadariyya.

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r6.speaker: المعتزلي
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r6.claim: Muʿtazila instead call determinists Qadariyya, because they say God decreed their adultery and theft; each side applies the label to its opponent.

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r7.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r7.claim: Both camps also label Sunnis Qadariyya for affirming God's creation of acts rather than their creation by the servant.
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r7.anchor: وهما جميعا يقولان لأهل السنة الذي يعترف بخلق الله وليس من العبد إنه قدري

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r8.claim: Razi identifies the Qadariyya meant here as those who deny divine decree and attribute events to the stars and their conjunctions; the Quraysh context and their denial of God's power to feed support this, unlike the Muʿtazilite account of human capacity.
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r8.anchor: والحق أن القدري الذي نزلت فيه الآية هو الذي ينكر القدر ويقول بأن الحوادث كلها حادثة بالكواكب واتصالاتها

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r9.claim: If umma means everyone to whom Muhammad was sent, including unbelievers, the contemporary Qadariyya were polytheists denying God's power over events, so the hadith does not include Muʿtazila.
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r9.anchor: فإن كان المراد الأول فالقدرية في زمانه هم المشركون الذين أنكروا قدرة الله على الحوادث فلا يدخل فيهم المعتزلة

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r10.claim: If umma means believers, the hadith compares one subgroup of this community to the Magi within the earlier community; it marks their weaker argument but does not prove they are certainly in Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r10.anchor: المجوس نوع منهم أضعف شبهة وأشد مخالفة للعقل

RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r11.claim: Razi concludes that Qadariyya means either deniers of God's power, if the name denotes negation, or those affirming another power over events; in either case he says their verse is error and their fate is Saqar.
RAZI-FULL:v29p61#4/r11.anchor: فالحق أن القدري هو الذي ينكر قدرة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r1.claim: The common reading links the verse to the preceding command to taste Saqar: the criminals are told to taste it because everything was created according to measure, in recompense for denying that doctrine.

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r2.claim: Razi prefers treating the verse as a new statement after the command to taste Saqar: the next verse pairs creation with God's command, as does 7:54, and thus confirms the new topic continues.
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r2.anchor: والظاهر أنه ابتداء كلام وتم الكلام

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r3.claim: Razi answers that the Prophet argued from the preceding punishment verses through ذوقوا مس سقر, then recited another verse without reading the final clause, relying on listeners to know it; he compares this to citing only part of other verses.
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#2/r3.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تمسك عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r1.claim: The common, sounder reading puts كل in the accusative; Razi parses it as the object of an omitted verb repeated by خلقناه, like the constructions in 36:39 and 76:31.

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r2.claim: On that parse the meaning is We created every thing according to measure; خلقناه is not an adjective here, though the comparable phrase in 51:49 is adjectival because it has no pronoun obstacle.
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r2.anchor: وخلقناه على هذا لا يكون صفة لشيء

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r3.claim: Because human acts are things, this accusative parse makes them included among everything created by God and thus refutes the Muʿtazila.
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا فالآية حجة على المعتزلة لأن أفعالنا شيء فتكون داخلة في كل شيء

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r4.claim: A nominative reading is also reported; Ibn Atiyya gives two syntactic analyses and notes that the Muʿtazili uses the nominative reading as an argument.
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r4.anchor: وهذان الوجهان ذكرهما ابن عطية في تفسيره وذكر أن المعتزلي يتمسك بقراءة الرفع

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r5.claim: The initial analysis of the nominative reading says the indefinite كل شيء cannot be a subject, requiring the sense every thing we created is by measure, as in 13:8; it cannot be parsed like the nominative reading in 41:17.

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r6.claim: A second accusative analysis takes the verb as understood rather than repeated from the apparent wording: either We created everything we created by measure, or We measured everything we created by measure.
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r6.anchor: معلوم لا بمضمر مفسر وهو قدرنا أو خلقنا

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r7.claim: Razi supports this understood verb from 40:62, God is creator of everything, and 13:8, everything is with a measure.

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r8.claim: On this parse, Razi says the verse does not refute the Muʿtazila but instead counts against the proposition he quotes as God is creator of everything.
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r8.anchor: وحينئذ لا يكون في الآية دلالة على بطلان قول المعتزلي

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r9.claim: For the nominative reading, كل شيء can be the subject and خلقناه بقدر its predicate, making the argument against the Muʿtazila especially strong.
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r9.anchor: جاز أن يكون كل شيء مبتدأ وخلقناه بقدر خبره

RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r10.claim: Razi rejects the objection that an indefinite cannot be a subject: كل شيء conveys universal scope and useful information, unlike bare رجل قائم; that is why ما أحد خير منك is acceptable while أحد خير منك is not.
RAZI-FULL:v29p64#3/r10.anchor: ولهذا جوزوا ما أحد خير منك

RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r1.claim: One sense of qadar is measure: things have measure in their essences and properties, including bodily extension, countable atoms, and finite limits in non-extended qualities such as knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r1.anchor: فكل شيء مقدر في ذاته وفي صفاته

RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r2.claim: Created things also have a measure of duration: each originated thing has a beginning and finite persistence, whereas God has neither measure nor beginning.
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r2.anchor: ولا مقدار له ولا ابتداء لوجوده

RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r3.claim: Although God is not measured or originated, the construction excludes the speaker by its compositional scope, as ordinary phrases about everyone in a house exclude the speaker; it does not exclude Him for lacking the predicate.

RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r4.claim: A second sense is determination, supported by 77:23 and a poetic line; God creates according to a prior measure rather than like an archer whose arrow lands somewhere unintended.
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا فالمعنى أن الله تعالى لم يخلق شيئا من غير تقدير

RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r5.claim: This determination opposes philosophers who say God acts by nature and outcomes vary only with matter's receptivity; Razi says small things could have been made large and large things small by God's measure.
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r5.anchor: بل خلق الله كما قدر بخلاف قول الفلاسفة إنه فاعل لذاته والاختلاف للقوابل

RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r6.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r6.claim: A third usage is qadar paired with qada: philosophers call the intended effect qada and what necessarily follows it qadar, as fire's heat and its burning of cotton or reeds.
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r6.anchor: ما يقصد إليه فقضاء وما يلزمه فقدر

RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p65/r7.claim: Razi rejects the philosophers' distinction as false: qada is God's knowledge and qadar His will, so the verse says all things are created according to His determination and will, against the polytheists.

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r1.claim: The verses are reported as revealed during the Prophet’s dispute with Quraysh idolaters over qadar, God’s allocation of provision to creation.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r1.anchor: reported to have been revealed in connection with a dispute between the Prophet and the idolaters among the Quraysh concerning God’s “measuring out”

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r2.claim: Here qadar, or measuring out, concerns how God gives or withholds provision for all creation.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r2.anchor: which refers to the manner in which God gives or withholds provision for all of creation

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r9.claim: The verse straightforwardly affirms that God created all things.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r9.anchor: This verse can be understood as a straightforward affirmation of God’s creation of all things

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r10.claim: In context, the measure may be the punishment God decreed for disbelievers and their casting into Saqar.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r10.anchor: In relation to the preceding verses, it can also be understood as a simple statement that God decreed or “measured” a punishment for the disbelievers and cast them into Saqar

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r11.claim: The Prophet’s debate with qadar-deniers made this verse a focus of the dispute over Divine determinism and human choice.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r11.anchor: this verse became a focal point for discussing the relation between Divine determinism and human choice

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r12.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r12.claim: The Prophet makes belief in qadar, good and evil, and acceptance of what befalls or misses one a condition of true faith.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r12.anchor: the Prophet said, “No servant of God truly believes until he believes in qadar, its good and evil

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r13.speaker: Jabariyyah
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r13.claim: The Jabariyyah hold that God determines every human act, including belief, disbelief, good, and evil; they cite 76:30 and 81:29.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r13.anchor: The earliest determinists, known as the Jabariyyah (lit. “Compulsionists”), held that all human acts were determined by God

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r14.claim: Exegetes favoring more human choice stress the precision or perfection of creation’s measure.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r14.anchor: those who favored a greater degree of human choice or self-determination preferred to focus upon the manner in which God has created everything with precision

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r15.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r15.claim: Most commentators and all recitation schools read kull shayʾ in the accusative, the translation’s form, though it is grammatically problematic.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r15.anchor: the reading preferred by most commentators and found in all schools of recitation

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r16.claim: Reading kull shayʾ in the nominative makes the phrase mean that everything God created is according to a measure.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r16.anchor: If, however, kull shayʾ is read in the nominative ( kullu shayʾin ), the verse could be understood to mean

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r17.claim: The nominative reading can leave open whether God created everything, supporting a free-will reading associated with Qadarites and Muʿtazilites.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r17.anchor: the early Qadarite theological trend and the Muʿtazilite school of theology

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r18.speaker: Qadarites
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r18.claim: Qadarites hold that humans are free and author their acts without thereby limiting God’s Omnipotence.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r18.anchor: The Qadarites held that human beings are free and are the authors of their own acts

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r19.speaker: Muʿtazilites
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r19.claim: Muʿtazilites hold humans responsible for creating their evil deeds, absolving a just God from creating acts for which He punishes them.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r19.anchor: The Muʿtazilites held that human beings are fully responsible for the creation of their evil deeds

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r20.speaker: Ashʿarite school of theology
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r20.claim: Ashʿarites reject Qadarite and Muʿtazilite creators outside God and Jabarite fatalism; God creates all acts while humans remain responsible, as 40:62 affirms.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r20.anchor: The Ashʿarite school of theology finds both of these positions abhorrent, because each would posit a creative agent outside of God
