STUDYQURAN:54:47/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r21.speaker: Ashʿarite theologians
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r21.claim: Ashʿarites distinguish God’s creation of acts from human acquisition: people choose among God-created options and thereby acquire their acts.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r21.anchor: Ashʿarite theologians thus sought to explain that God is Just and Merciful and does not punish people for things for which they are not responsible

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r22.speaker: commentators favoring Muʿtazilite views
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r22.claim: Free-will leaning commentators do not use this verse to prove their position; they emphasize Divine Wisdom in the universe’s precise measure.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r22.anchor: Commentators who incline more toward the Muʿtazilite position and favor a greater degree of free will than that allowed for by the Ashʿarite position

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r23.speaker: al-Zamakhsharī
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r23.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says creation follows wisdom’s determined measure, or a measure written on the Tablet and known by God before existence, including its state and duration.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r23.anchor: al-Zamakhsharī writes, “We have created everything in a determined measure, ordered according to that which wisdom has decreed

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r24.speaker: al-Ṭabrisī
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r24.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī says nothing is haphazard: each thing has a known measure and purpose, and changing its measure would defeat its function.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r24.anchor: the Shiite theologian al-Ṭabrisī emphasizes that this verse indicates that nothing has been created haphazardly

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r25.speaker: Ashʿarites
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r25.claim: Ashʿarite commentators see Divine Wisdom and the Preserved Tablet here; humans acquire acts but cannot create or determine them, while vv. 47–48 criticize those claims.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r25.anchor: Many who are more closely aligned with the Ashʿarite position also see this verse as an expression of the Divine Wisdom

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r26.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r26.speaker: Ashʿarites
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r26.claim: Ashʿarites cite a hadith calling the community’s qadar-deniers its Magians.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r26.anchor: they cite several aḥādīth, among them: “Every community has its Magians, and the Magians of my community are those who say that there is no measuring out

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r27.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r27.speaker: Ashʿarites
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r27.claim: Ashʿarites distinguish pretemporal qaḍāʾ, pertaining to God’s uncreated Essence, from temporal qadar, an attribute of Action contingent with what it brings into being.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r27.anchor: In elaborating upon their understanding of Divine determinism, Ashʿarites identify two stages or aspects of the Divine Decree

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r28.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r28.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r28.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects philosophical necessity: qaḍāʾ concerns God’s Knowledge and qadar His Will, so creation occurs by His willing measure rather than necessity.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r28.anchor: al-Rāzī argues against the philosophical notion that it is necessary for things to be created in the manner that they are created

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r29.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r29.speaker: Ibn ʿAjībah
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r29.claim: Ibn ʿAjībah says certainty in the measure relieves sorrow and planning, leading one to entrust affairs to God and accept every decree; he alludes to 102:5 and 40:44.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r29.anchor: Thus Ibn ʿAjībah writes: “It washes the heart of sorrows and of all that is other

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r30.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r30.speaker: al-Maybudī
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r30.claim: Al-Maybudī says finding God means having everything, while a person deprived of God has nothing despite possessing everything.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r30.anchor: In this same vein, the commentator al-Maybudī writes of this verse

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r31.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r31.speaker: Sufi thinkers
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r31.claim: Ibn ʿArabī’s and Mullā Ṣadrā’s schools relate choice and Decree to humanity’s capacity to know the Divine Names, including al-Murīd and al-Qadīr; freedom is itself God-created.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r31.anchor: For many Sufi thinkers, such as those of the school of Ibn ʿArabī

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r32.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r32.speaker: Sufi thinkers
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r32.claim: Sufis see human will as God’s Power and Will manifested, and true freedom as a state attained by rising above ego and submitting one’s individual will to God.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r32.anchor: Rather than seeing the question of human free will as a question merely of choices between options on a particular plane of reality

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r33.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r33.speaker: Ibn ʿArabī
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r33.claim: Ibn ʿArabī’s paradox is that saints most able to perform miracles are least likely to do so because they accept God’s Will.
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r33.anchor: This is exemplified in a paradox discussed by Ibn ʿArabī, who says that those saints

STUDYQURAN:54:47/r34.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r34.speaker: Sufi thinkers
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r34.claim: Sufis understand one’s qadar or lot as one’s essence known by God before creation; God transcends free-will and determinism, while human freedom originates in God’s breathing His Spirit into Adam (32:9).
STUDYQURAN:54:47/r34.anchor: Moreover, qadar, or one’s “lot,” is seen, in the ultimate sense, as a manifestation of one’s own nature or essence as known by God before one’s creation

TAB-FULL:v22p162/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r1.claim: God created everything according to a measure He determined and decreed; the verse threatens the criminals for denying divine decree alongside their disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، " أن مشركي، قريش خاصمت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في القدر، فأنزل الله {إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر}

TAB-FULL:v22p162/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas recalls people dragged face down through the Fire and told to taste Saqar because they denied decree; he wonders whether they belonged to the past or future.
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه كان يقول: «إني أجد في كتاب الله قوما يسحبون في النار على وجوههم، يقال لهم» : {ذوقوا مس سقر}

TAB-FULL:v22p162/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed with the Prophet about decree, whereupon this verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، " أن مشركي، قريش خاصمت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في القدر، فأنزل الله {إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر}

TAB-FULL:v22p162/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r4.claim: A second wording from Abu Hurayra says the dispute over decree occasioned the revelation of the preceding warning about criminals in error and the decree verse.
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: «جاء مشركو قريش إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاصمونه في القدر، فنزلت» {إن المجرمين في ضلال وسعر}

TAB-FULL:v22p162/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r5.claim: After the verse was revealed, a man asked whether deeds are newly undertaken or already settled; the Prophet replied to act, since each person is facilitated for what they were created for.
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r5.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية {إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر} [القمر: 49] قال رجل: يا رسول الله ففيم العمل؟

TAB-FULL:v22p162/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says the passage describing criminals in error through the decree verse was revealed concerning people debating divine decree.
TAB-FULL:v22p162/r6.anchor: سمعت محمد بن كعب القرظي، يقول: " لما تكلم الناس في القدر نظرت، فإذا هذه الآية أنزلت فيهم

TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says the verse was revealed as a rebuke to deniers of decree, quoting the warning to taste Saqar.
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r1.anchor: عن سالم، عن محمد بن كعب قال: " ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا تعييرا لأهل القدر {ذوقوا مس سقر

TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra again reports that Quraysh challenged the Prophet over decree and this verse was revealed in response.
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: " جاء مشركو قريش إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاصمونه في القدر، فنزلت: {إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر}

TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God created all creatures by decree and created good and evil by decree; the best good is happiness and the worst evil is wretchedness.
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر} [القمر: 49] قال: «خلق الله الخلق كلهم بقدر، وخلق لهم الخير والشر بقدر

TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r4.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r4.claim: Some Basran grammarians explain the accusative كل as the pattern in “Abd Allah, I struck him”; they also allow nominative forms, including treating خلقناه as an adjective of شيء.
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r4.anchor: قال بعض نحويي البصرة: نصب كل شيء في لغة من قال: عبد الله ضربته؛ قال: وهي في كلام العرب كثير

TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r5.speaker: غيره
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r5.claim: Another grammarian says كل is accusative because the verb خلقناه has stronger claim to precedence after إنا than the object, unlike the dislocated object in the comparison.
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r5.anchor: وقال غيره: إنما نصب كل لأن قوله خلقناه فعل، لقوله «إنا» ، وهو أولى بالتقديم إليه من المفعول

TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the second grammarian's explanation and rejects treating خلقناه as an adjective of شيء because that produces the less apt meaning “We created it every thing by measure.”
TAB-FULL:v22p162#2/r6.anchor: وهذا القول الثاني أولى بالصواب عندي من الأول للعلل التي ذكرت لصاحبه

SULAMI:v2p291/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p291/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p291/r1.claim: Al-Qasim says God's measure encompasses every soul, deed, trace, thought, breath, moment, trait, lifespan, and livelihood, displaying prior knowledge and power; none escapes His decree or the execution of His will.
SULAMI:v2p291/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : دخل في هذا المعنى نفوس الخلق واعمالهم وآثارهم وخطرت قلوبهم وأنفاسهم في اوقاتهم وأخلاقهم المحمودة

SULAMI:v2p291/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p291/r2.speaker: يوسف بن الحسين
SULAMI:v2p291/r2.claim: Yusuf ibn al-Husayn states a principle of predestination: the divine decree prevails over our resolve.
SULAMI:v2p291/r2.anchor: سمعت يوسف بن الحسين وقد سئل عن شيء من القدر فقال : من اصولنا أن القضاء امضى بنا من عزمنا .

TABATABAI:54:45-49/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:45-49/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:45-49/r8.claim: ‘Everything’ is the object of an implicit verb supplied by ‘We created’; the preposition in ‘by measure’ attaches to ‘created,’ and the bāʾ indicates accompaniment.

TABATABAI:54:45-49/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:45-49/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:45-49/r9.claim: Qadar is each thing’s determined measure and limit, which it cannot exceed in either increase or decrease.
TABATABAI:54:45-49/r9.anchor: وقدر الشيء هو المقدار الذي لا يتعداه والحد والهندسة التي لا يتجاوزه

TABATABAI:54:49/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:49/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:49/r1.claim: As 15:21 says that everything is held in God’s treasuries and sent down by a known measure, every thing has a defined limit and a path it follows in existence.
TABATABAI:54:49/r1.anchor: فلكل شيء حد محدود في خلقه لا يتعداه وصراط ممدود في وجوده يسلكه

TABATABAI:54:49/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:49/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:49/r2.claim: The measure answers why criminals are punished: human beings are a reproducing social species made for transient worldly life and eternal life beyond it; God sends messengers, and accepting or rejecting their call is measured to lead to Paradise or punishment.
TABATABAI:54:49/r2.anchor: فمن استجاب الدعوة فاز بالسعادة ودخل الجنة

TABATABAI:54:49/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:49/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:49/r3.claim: The reply is not circular: human actions follow general rules inferred from external existence and learned effects, such as eating to satisfy hunger and drinking to quench thirst.
TABATABAI:54:49/r3.anchor: فإنا نتبع في أفعالنا القوانين والأصول الكلية المأخوذة من الكون الخارجي والوجود العيني

TABATABAI:54:49#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r1.claim: God’s acts are not governed by an external cause or prior universal rational rule: such rules are derived from His act and are subordinate to it, as the cited verses affirm.
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r1.anchor: فلا سؤال عن فعله تعالى بلم بمعنى السؤال عن السبب الخارجي إذ لا سبب دونه يعينه في فعله

TABATABAI:54:49#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r2.claim: First, God’s acts can be explained by their benefits to creatures; this explains the act within causal relations, not why God acts as God. The author illustrates this with the cited verses on Christian affection and Israel’s humiliation.
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r2.anchor: تعليل الفعل بما يترتب عليه من الغايات والفوائد العائدة إلى الخلق لا إليه

TABATABAI:54:49#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r3.claim: Second, a particular act can be explained through a fitting divine name or attribute; such active names are drawn from God’s general acts, so the particular is explained by a general feature of divine action.
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r3.anchor: تعليل فعله تعالى بشيء من أسمائه وصفاته المناسبة له

TABATABAI:54:49#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r4.claim: Third, the specific punishment in 54:47–49 is explained by God’s general act of measuring all things: the criminal’s punishment is one instance of the measure set for a person who rejects prophecy.
TABATABAI:54:49#2/r4.anchor: فإن القدر وهو كون الشيء محدودا لا يتخطى حده

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r1.claim: The Quran describes creation as measured and guided in several formulations: God measured everything, gave each thing its form and then guided it, and holds all things in measure.

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r2.claim: Qadar has two levels: a universal limit on the possible, dependent existence of every being except God, and a particular limit on observable beings shaped by their causes and conditions.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r2.anchor: للتقدير مرتبتين مرتبة تعم جميع ما سوى الله وهي تحديد أصل الوجود بالإمكان والحاجة

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r3.claim: In the observable world, external and internal causes and conditions shape each thing’s existence, effects, form, dimensions, states, and actions; this measure guides it along its assigned course.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r3.anchor: فهي مقلوبة بقوالب من داخل وخارج تعين لها من العرض والطول والشكل والهيئة

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r4.claim: The statement that God created, proportioned, measured, and guided each thing means He guides what He created along the course measured for it.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r4.anchor: أي هدى ما خلقه إلى ما قدر له

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r5.claim: For human beings, being created from a drop, measured, and then having the path made easy shows that qadar does not negate voluntary action.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r5.anchor: ويشير بقوله { ثم السبيل يسره } إلى أن التقدير لا ينافي

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r6.claim: This form of qadar differs from qada, God’s decisive judgment that something exist, which no one can reverse.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r6.anchor: وهذا النوع من القدر في نفسه غير القضاء الذي هو الحكم البتي منه تعالى بوجوده

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r7.claim: A measure implied by some causes or conditions may fail to reach actualization because an impediment intervenes or another cause replaces it; the Quran calls this erasing and confirming.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r7.anchor: فربما قدر ولم يعقبه القضاء كالقدر الذي يقتضيه بعض العلل والشرائط الخارجة

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r8.claim: When every cause and condition is assembled and all impediments are absent, qadar is followed by qada.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r8.anchor: وربما قدر وتبعه القضاء كما إذا قدر من جميع الجهات باجتماع جميع علله وشرائطه وارتفاع موانعه

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r9.speaker: الإمام
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r9.claim: A report in al-Mahasin says that when God decrees something He carries it out, and that outcome cannot be averted; other reports likewise distinguish changeable qadar from irreversible qada.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r9.anchor: إذا قضى أمضاه فذلك الذي لا مرد له

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r10.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r10.claim: Ibn Nubata reports that when Ali moved from a leaning wall to another, he answered that he was fleeing God’s qada to God’s qadar.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r10.anchor: أفر من قضاء الله إلى قدر الله عز وجل

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r11.claim: For beings whose measure is only the limit of possibility and need, qadar and qada are identical and the measure necessarily comes to pass.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r11.anchor: فالقدر والقضاء فيه واحد ولا يتخلف القدر فيه عن التحقق البتة

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r12.claim: Rationally, each element of a composite cause (agent, matter, conditions, preparations, and impediments) contributes a matching effect that shapes the thing’s measure; when the complete cause forms, existence becomes necessary, which is qada.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r12.anchor: وهذه هي القضاء الذي لا مرد له

TABATABAI:54:43-55/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r13.claim: For a useful earlier discussion of qada, the author refers readers to his commentary at the beginning of Surat al-Isra.
TABATABAI:54:43-55/r13.anchor: وقد تقدم في تفسير أول سورة الإسراء كلام في القضاء

AKHFASH:v2p529/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p529/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p529/r2.claim: The accusative كل follows the Arabic pattern of fronting an object resumed by a pronoun, as in عبد الله ضربته, a common construction.
AKHFASH:v2p529/r2.anchor: وأما نصب {كل} ففي لغة من قال "عبد الله ضربته" وهو في كلام العرب كثير

AKHFASH:v2p529/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p529/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p529/r3.claim: He also records raising كل in a usage that raises it, and another way of parsing it in the nominative.
AKHFASH:v2p529/r3.anchor: وقد رفعت "كل" في لغة من رفع ورفعت على وجه آخر

AKHFASH:v2p529/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p529/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p529/r4.claim: In the further analysis, خلقناه is treated as an adjective qualifying شيء.
AKHFASH:v2p529/r4.anchor: قال {إنا كل شيء خلقناه} فجعل {خلقناه} من صفة الشيء

TABRISI:54:49/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:49/r2.speaker: أبو السماك
TABRISI:54:49/r2.claim: In a noncanonical reading, Abu al-Sammak reads anna with nominative kullu; the main reading has accusative kulla.
TABRISI:54:49/r2.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة أبي السماك أنا كل شيء بالرفع

TABRISI:54:49/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:49/r4.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:54:49/r4.claim: Ibn Jinni prefers nominative kullu as a topic with a clause predicate, like “Zayd, I struck him”; innā changes the noun's case while the clause retains its structure.
TABRISI:54:49/r4.anchor: قال ابن جني الرفع في قوله

TABRISI:54:49/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:49/r5.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
TABRISI:54:49/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid prefers accusative kullā, supplying an understood verb after innā from the preceding context.
TABRISI:54:49/r5.anchor: واختيار محمد بن يزيد النصب لأن تقديره إنا فعلنا كذا

TABRISI:54:49/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:49/r6.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:54:49/r6.claim: Ibn Jinni rejects al-Mubarrid's argument: a nominal sentence's predicate is originally a noun, not a separate verb, and inna's predicate follows the same principle.
TABRISI:54:49/r6.anchor: قال ابن جني وهذا ليس بشيء لأن الأصل في خبر المبتدأ أن يكون اسما

TABRISI:54:49-52/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:49-52/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:54:49-52/r6.claim: Al-Jubba'i says God creates each thing according to a measure required by wisdom, never aimlessly; punishment is proportioned to deserts and all things are measured.
TABRISI:54:49-52/r6.anchor: خلقنا كل شيء خلقناه مقدرا بمقدار توجبه الحكمة لم نخلقه جزافا

TABRISI:54:49-52/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:49-52/r7.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:54:49-52/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says each thing has a proper measured function: the tongue speaks, hand grasps, foot walks, eye sees, ear hears, and stomach digests food.
TABRISI:54:49-52/r7.anchor: فخلقنا اللسان للكلام واليد للبطش والرجل للمشي والعين للنظر

TABRISI:54:49-52/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:49-52/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:54:49-52/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets qadar as fitting forms paired appropriately, such as woman and man, she-ass and donkey, and men's and women's clothing.
TABRISI:54:49-52/r8.anchor: جعلنا لكل شيء شكلا يوافقه ويصلح له كالمرأة للرجل والأتان للحمار

TABRISI:54:49-52/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:49-52/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:54:49-52/r9.claim: Another view takes qadar as a fixed measure and decree recorded in the Preserved Tablet.
TABRISI:54:49-52/r9.anchor: وقيل: خلقنا كل شيء بقدر مقدر وقضاء محتوم في اللوح المحفوظ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r1.speaker: الكلبي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r1.claim: One reading says God made each thing in a form suited to it, such as woman to man, she-ass to donkey, mare to horse, and gender-appropriate clothing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي عن ابن عباس: إنا كل شيء جعلنا له شكلا يوافقه ويصلح له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says God assigned each created thing its proper measure, as in 65:3; al-Rabiʿ agrees.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: قدر الله لكل شيء من خلقه قدره الذي ينبغي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r3.claim: Muqatil interprets the verse as God having decreed punishment for the criminals, linking it to what precedes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني أنه قدر لهم العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r4.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says 54:45–49 was revealed concerning the Qadariyya after Quraysh's polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن # قوله: {إن المجرمين}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi also says the passage was revealed to rebuke the Qadariyya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r5.anchor: وهذا قول محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: نزلت تعييرا لأهل القدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r6.claim: On the Qadariyya interpretation, the criminals are the polytheist deniers of predestination and their counterparts in this community, who share their status.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا القول المراد بالمجرمين القدرية المشركون وإخوانهم من قدرية هذه الأمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r7.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet recited these verses and said they were revealed concerning people in the later community who deny God's decree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r7.anchor: أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قرأ هذه الآيات وقال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r8.speaker: أبو ذر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r8.claim: Abu Dharr reports that a delegation from Najran asked whether deeds were theirs while lifespans belonged to God; after asking why they would be punished for written sins, the Prophet called them God's disputants on Judgment Day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r8.anchor: وروي عن أبي ذر قال: قدم وقد نجران على النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- فقالوا: الأعمال إلينا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r9.speaker: النبي عن عمر بن الخطاب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r9.claim: The Prophet said a herald will summon God's disputants on Judgment Day, meaning the Qadariyya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r9.anchor: ويؤكد هذا ما روى عمر بن الخطاب -رضي الله عنه- عن رسول -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r10.speaker: كعب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r10.claim: Kaʿb says the Torah states that the Qadariyya will be dragged face-down in the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r10.anchor: ويزيد وضوحا هذه الجملة ما روي عن كعب أنه قال: نجد في التوراة أن القدرية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r11.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r11.claim: Ata attributes to Ibn Abbas the report that the verses were revealed about polytheist Qadariyya who argued with the Messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p123/r11.anchor: وهو قول عطاء عن ابن عباس أن الآيات نزلت في القدرية من المشركين الذين جادلوا رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p125/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p125/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p125/r1.claim: On the predestination reading, everything created is measured and written in the Preserved Tablet before it occurs, supported by 54:52.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p125/r1.anchor: يدل على هذا قوله: {وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر} ذكر ذلك أبو إسحاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p125/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p125/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p125/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God created all beings according to decree and created good and evil for them; the best good is felicity and the worst evil is wretchedness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p125/r2.anchor: وروى الوالبي عن ابن عباس قال: خلق الله الخلق كلهم بقدر، وخلق لهم الخير والشر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:49-55/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:49-55/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:49-55/r1.claim: Everything God creates is measured and recorded in the Preserved Tablet.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:49-55/r1.anchor: إن كل شيء خلقناه بقدر } أي: كل ما خلقناه فمقدور مكتوب في اللوح المحفوظ

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:49-55/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:49-55/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:49-55/r2.claim: These verses were revealed about the Qadariyya, who deny divine decree.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:49-55/r2.anchor: وهذه الآيات نزلت في القدرية الذين يكذبون بالقدر

ELMALILI:54:43-55/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r14.claim: Everything has a measure determined in God’s eternal knowledge before it occurs, and its actual creation takes place according to it.
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r14.anchor: haysiyyet-i ilmiyesi vardır ki kazâsının cereyânı, fiilen yaratılışı o kadere göre vâki‘olur.

ELMALILI:54:43-55/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r15.claim: No other agent can determine or necessitate a thing’s measure as it pleases.
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r15.anchor: Onu başkası istediği gibi îcab ve tâyin (determine)

ELMALILI:54:43-55/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r16.claim: A criminal cannot change sin’s nature or appointed outcome to suit desire; wrongdoing destined for misery and hell cannot become a path to happiness.
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r16.anchor: için mücrim, kendi keyif ve iradesine göre cürmün mâhiyet ve mukadderâtını değiştiremez.

ELMALILI:54:43-55/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r17.claim: Because their crimes bring accountability and misery, criminals remain in error and fire rather than converting sin into felicity.
ELMALILI:54:43-55/r17.anchor: Kaderde âkıbeti bedbahtlık, mes’ûliyet, mahkûmiyet ile cehenneme götürmek olan cürm ü me‘âsî sevab ve saadet vesilesi yapılamaz.

ELMALILI:54:43-55#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:43-55#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:43-55#2/r1.claim: Divine decree does not cancel human partial will: voluntary acts occurring through that will are themselves included in qadar.

MAJAZ:v1p9/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p9/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p9/r2.claim: A plural form can carry a singular meaning: ‘the people’ in 3:173 was one speaker, and the ‘we’ who create in 54:49 is God alone; ‘I am your Lord’s messenger’ is another example.
MAJAZ:v1p9/r2.anchor: ومن مجاز ما جاء لفظه لفظ الجميع الذي له واحد منه، ووقع معنى هذا الجميع على الواحد، قال:

MAJAZ:v1p9/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p9/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p9/r4.claim: He begins a further category in which a word has no separate plural form, so the singular and plural forms are identical; its example is not present in this excerpt.
MAJAZ:v1p9/r4.anchor: ومن مجاز ما جاء لا جماع له من لفظه فلفظ الواحد منه ولفظ الجميع سواء

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r1.claim: One gloss of creating everything by measure is that it is made according to wisdom, firmly, and within a defined order and balance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r1.anchor: “her şeyin hikmetin gereklerine uygun biçimde, sağlam, belli bir düzen ve denge içinde”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r2.claim: Another gloss is that each thing is created according to the form already known and recorded in God's eternal knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r2.anchor: “Allah’ın ezelî ilminde mâlûm ve kayıtlı olan şekle göre” mânalarıyla açıklanmıştır (Zemahşerî, IV, 48-49).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r3.claim: Read with the next statement about God's command occurring instantly, the passage stresses that no power can determine or affect God's will, no time or place constrains Him, and His power has no limit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:49/r3.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah’ın iradesini belirleyecek veya etkileyecek hiçbir güç bulunmadığı gibi, O’nun için zaman, mekân vb. faktörlerin söz konusu olmadığına ve kudretine sınır düşünülemeyeceğine vurgu

TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.claim: Verses on divine measure show things descending from undetermined plenitude into particular existence by a determination that precedes and accompanies them, including their relations to other existents.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.anchor: تدل على أن الأشياء تنزل من ساحة الإطلاق إلى مرحلة التعين والتشخص بتقدير منه تعالى

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed with the Messenger about divine decree, prompting the passage from “the criminals are in error” through “We created everything according to a measure.”
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال جاء مشركو قريش يخاصمون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في القدر فنزلت

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh disputed predestination, after which verses 54:47–49 were revealed; al-Wahidi notes that Muslim transmitted the report.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: جاءت قريش يختصمون في القدر، فأنزل الله تعالى:

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r3.claim: Abu Umama al-Bahili attributes to the Prophet a statement that the passage about criminals in error and measure was revealed regarding the Qadariyya.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r3.anchor: سمعت أبا أمامة الباهلي يقول: أشهد بالله لسمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول:
